description_full: Stagwell Inc. provides digital transformation, marketing, media and commerce, marketing cloud, and communications services in the United States, the United Kingdom, and internationally. The company offers creative, research, experiential, and social media solutions designed to build and elevate brands; and consumer insights through advanced research methodologies, creating immersive experiential marketing programs and social engagement strategies that connect brands with audiences across digital platforms. It also designs, implements, and activates digital ecosystems that enable brand and customer experiences through the integration of strategy, design, and technology; provides managed services, staff augmentation, and engineering expertise across various delivery models, offering system integration, full-stack development, and ongoing platform management; and provides digital transformation that connects digital ecosystems to physical experiences through innovative, technology-driven customer engagements. In addition, the company offers integrated AI-based data solutions that drive audience engagement and business growth through media buying, owned media platforms, commerce enablement, and customer relationship management strategies; specialized media platforms and translation services to support targeted communication and market expansion; an edge set of solutions designed to help organizations build, protect, and enhance their reputation across diverse audiences and channels; and expertise in targeted communications, crisis management, and stakeholder engagement services. Further, the company provides a suite of technology solutions for in-house marketers and combining SaaS and DaaS offerings. Stagwell Inc. was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

Each employee generates $23K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $5K per employee reflects an ownership culture. financial_summary: Stagwell Inc. is a mid-cap communication services business with a $2.9B market cap on $2.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $247M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 10.00× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 1.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 59% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
